messages: Break the grip of concentrated economic power. That concern shapes much of how I approach agriculture, banking, healthcare, wages, antitrust policy, and the economy more broadly. I want an economy where family farmers, workers, entrepreneurs, and small businesses can compete without being overwhelmed by institutions with enormous financial and political power.

Government should serve working people rather than powerful institutions. I believe our government should answer to the people it represents—not corporations, wealthy donors, lobbyists, or Wall Street. I care deeply about family farmers, workers, small businesses, families, and retirees. That is also why I am concerned about the influence of campaign money, congressional stock trading, lobbying, conflicts of interest, and the increasingly close relationship between corporate and political power.

Put American security and long-term prosperity ahead of entrenched interests. I believe we need to think seriously about what kind of country we are leaving to the next generation. That means reducing the risk of unnecessary wars and nuclear escalation, protecting Social Security and Medicare, confronting climate change, and taking seriously the economic and social consequences of rapidly expanding artificial intelligence and data centers. My focus is on the long-term security and prosperity of the American people rather than protecting institutions simply because they have become powerful or politically entrenched.

Families across Wisconsin are being squeezed by higher grocery bills, housing costs, utility bills, health care costs, and taxes while Washington keeps spending money it does not have. As such, I believe affordability should be the top priority in Congress, so I will fight to reduce wasteful federal spending, oppose policies that drive up everyday costs, ease burdens on small businesses and working families, and restore basic fiscal responsibility before politicians pass even more debt onto the next generation.

Government must be transparent, accountable, and limited. We have all watched politicians campaign as outsiders, go to Washington, and become the very machine they claimed to oppose. The incumbent is the perfect example: He explicitly promised he would not become a career politician, yet here he is, running again after years in Congress, breaking his own word. That hypocrisy is the problem. I am running to expose waste, directly challenge government overreach, and restore authority to the people—not the political class. I won’t go to Washington to join the club; I’m going there to disrupt it.

I am running as an Independent because the two-party system is too comfortable managing problems instead of solving them, and when the goal is just "winning the news cycle," the people lose every time. I am running to end this manufactured stalemate and bring an objective, fearless, and investigative eye to Congress. I will work with anyone serious about lowering costs, protecting individual rights, and restoring accountability—and I will fiercely oppose anyone, in either party, who puts partisan games ahead of Wisconsin families.

Politicians have sold out the American people to corporations and their billionaire donors. I am running as a firefighter and father of four to continue being a public servant and represent the great people of WI-06. Breaking up monopolies across industries that manipulate markets, price gouge consumers and producers, and crush the American dream. Making housing more affordable by expanding the supply, cutting back on regulations limiting housing development, and banning investment firms from buying single family homes and apartments. Making sure data centers not only pay for their own electricity and water use, but also invest in the energy grids that they utilize. These are all policy…

As a firefighter and HAZMAT specialist public safety is something I take very seriously. Politicians often speak about public safety and take pictures with our first responders, but when it comes time to make sure FEMA funding is disbursed on time they are no where to be found. I am running to make sure there is local input in our public safety work. Additionally, Monopolies have taken over the production of emergency service equipment price-gouging the tax payer and slowing production. This means we waste millions in tax payer dollars on equipment and then often have to wait years to get these life saving machines.

My campaign is rooted in anti-corruption. For too long politicians from both parties have been enriching themselves through insider trading, crypto currency schemes, and major lobbying deals once they leave office. I would ban any trading of stocks or crypto currency by all elected officials, push for term limits to be enacted, and fight to ban corporate pac money from our elections.

messages: I am running for Wisconsin State Senate because the people of Wisconsin deserve a representative who shows up and fights for working and middle-class families, small business owners, and farmers. I want to help Wisconsin residents build a better economy that works for everyone, not just the wealthiest Wisconsinites and the big corporations. We need new ideas and big, bold changes. Establishment politics isn't working for Wisconsin anymore. I want to help the community that I love and make a positive impact that truly improves people's lives. I hope people will vote for a neighbor and a friend instead of a letter next to the unknown name of a stranger who doesn't show up for you or your…

I support fully funding our public schools and lowering property taxes. We had 7 public school referendums in the 13th district. We need our rural public schools. They are an integral part of our communities and our rural culture. Rural schools are important to our kids, parents, homeowners, school staff, and small businesses. We must elect legislators who will work to restructure the way we fund our public schools so they can once again provide the great education that our kids deserve and attract and retain the best educators, while also lowering our property taxes. We can’t continue placing such a high tax burden on our homeowners and we can’t tax our retired people out of their homes.

We need a pause on building data centers until we have strict regulations, transparency, and input from the public. We must elect legislators who will stand up to big corporations and fight to protect our rural communities, our natural resources, and our farms. We need to ensure that companies building data centers pay their fair share of taxes from the beginning and throughout the entirety of the project and pay 100% of the costs to build, maintain, and use the facilities. Wisconsin residents should not foot the bill for building new infrastructure, upgrading the electrical grid, or increasing gas, water, and electric rates. We must demand transparency and put an end to the use of NDA's…

I have a proven track record of fighting for the priorities of the 15th District, providing excellent constituent services, and showing up to public events to meet people where they are. I’m running for re-election because there is more work to be done, and I am already a legislative leader on many of the most pressing issues facing our district, including housing, AI and data center regulation, supporting our family farms, and reducing the burden of property taxes. I serve as the Senate Democratic Caucus Chair and am in a position to play a lead role in a Democratic majority. We must lower the cost of everyday needs, healthcare, childcare, and housing while supporting public schools and…

We need to tackle high prices by lowering the costs of childcare, healthcare, higher education, and housing. We should empower local communities to solve their most pressing challenges without overreliance on property taxes. We must stop the endless referendum cycle by investing in our local public schools so students get the education they deserve. We need to reduce the burden of property taxes and keep retirement affordable and accessible by expanding the Homestead Tax Credit. The high cost of living is the number one issue I hear about when talking to my constituents. While the state can’t do much about the national economy or the price of gas, we can do much more about the cost of…

We must protect people from the negative effects of hyperscale data centers. I’ve supported bills to ban government officials from signing NDAs with data center developers, make data centers, not rate-payers, pay for new power, and provide regulations around water, clean energy, labor protections, and more. I support repealing the sales tax exemption that is attracting hyperscale data centers to Wisconsin, and that has already cost us $2 billion in lost tax revenue. The majority of people simply do not want hyperscale data centers in their community, and many communities in my district are passing moratoriums at the local level. I support authorizing local communities to say No to data…

messages: Rooted in Community, Committed to Service I was born halfway across the world and adopted by my father, a fourth-generation Racinian and small business owner. I will always be a proud product of my hometown. After graduating from Racine Public School and the University of Wisconsin - Milwaukee, I came back to become the youngest person elected to the Racine Common Council in more than a century, where I worked to expand service access for working families and seniors. As Racine’s Transit Director, I have modernized the fleet and launched the city’s first transit app to better connect residents to work, school, healthcare, and opportunity. Now, I am running for State Senate to continue…

Build an Affordable Economy for Everybody Across Southeast Wisconsin, too many hardworking families are being squeezed as the price of everyday essential goods and services like gas, groceries and childcare rise faster than our wages. Too many young people feel they must leave home to find economic opportunity in another city or another state. I believe in building an economy that works for everyone, not just those at the top. That means attracting more jobs to our region and raising wages, taking on corporate consolidation to lower costs, and expanding access to apprenticeships and skills training in order to create real pathways to family-supporting careers right here at home so every…

A New Way For too long, Madison has asked our communities to wait their turn and settle for less. We pay our taxes like everyone else, yet we don’t see our fair share come back. We get less funding for our schools, less investment in our healthcare and infrastructure, and less opportunity for our working families to get ahead. I do not accept this status quo and will fight to change it. I will stand up for Southeast Wisconsin in the State Senate and make sure our money comes back to us — back into safer neighborhoods, better schools, better roads, and a brighter future for our young people. No more scraps from Madison — we will finally get our fair share. It’s time our communities get…

incumbents.name: Van Wanggaard
incumbents.note: Van Wanggaard (R–Racine), representing district 21 since 2015, is retiring.

messages: Freedom as a value we all share. Freedoms under threat include reproductive freedom, the freedom of citizens to vote in the least restrictive manner, and freedom from gun violence.
Family values. Our children deserve high quality daycare and the best public education possible. Families benefit from the security of paid medical leave.

Community as a value. Accessible and affordable health care is a human right. Young people should be able to see a future for themselves and a family in their hometowns. Incentivizing apprentices and graduates to stay in, or return to, their family farm or hometown will sustain and grow small communities. Farmers, manufacturers, and retail businesses keep communities vibrant. Investing in small communities will pay huge dividends.

incumbents.name: Jesse James
incumbents.note: Jesse James (R–Thorp), representing district 23 since 2023, is retiring.

messages: School funding is unfair and needs reform. The school funding formula has not been updated since 1993. It is time. Vouchers for private schools should not come from local school funds.

Healthcare is a right not a privilege. I support a Badger Care Buy-In option. I support State funding to help rural EMS. Elders deserve to age with dignity. I support programs that empower people in their homes - ARDCs, Meals on Wheels and support for care givers. I support locally owned elder facilities and have voted in support of our Bayfield County nursing home.

Madison need to support local decisions determining our land uses, protecting our property rights and protecting our environment. Madison should set minimum standards, not hold back local government from appropriate local decisions on development projects.

incumbents.name: Romaine Quinn
incumbents.note: Running for State Senator, District 23 instead.

messages: Reduce Taxes and return surplus money to the Taxpayer.
Protect your rights. Gun rights, Property rights.
Keep men out of womens sports.

I am an attorney and former congressional candidate with roots in small-town Wisconsin. I grew up in Somerset as the son of a truck driver and a secretary, experiences that shaped my understanding of work, responsibility, and economic opportunity. My background, as a college football player, lawyer, and parent, has informed my focus on practical problem-solving and accountability in public service.

My approach to public service is pragmatic and outcomes-focused. I believe effective government requires transparency, clear rules, and consistent enforcement to ensure fairness and prevent abuses of power. I believe that when government acts as a passive bystander rather than a referee, costs often increase for families and businesses due to reduced accountability and weakened competition. In my legal and public work, I try to emphasize institutional accountability and the equal application of rules to everybody, including those making the rules, as essential to trust and effective governance.

My policy priorities focus on long-term affordability for working families. When discussing wage growth and cost-of-living pressures, we need to focus on structural and systemic approaches rather than short-term spending increases alone. I believe in the role of competition, accountability, and effective oversight in shaping wages and prices, alongside efforts to reduce property tax pressures on families and improve transparency in government decision-making. Government has a role in ensuring robust competition is happening, a role it has shirked for the last 45 years.
We need our state legislature to address issues of basic affordability for Wisconsin residents: housing, healthcare and childcare.

Wisconsin needs to finally fix our public education funding formula. For years, both sides in Madison have agreed that our public school funding formula needs an overhaul, yet the Republican-controlled legislature has not taken any steps to fix it. Instead, Republicans have chosen to underfund public education year after year after year, leading to a historic numbers of school referendums and rising property taxes. Adding insult to injury, gerrymandering allowed Republicans to expand the voucher school program, essentially siphoning tax dollars to less accountable private and religious schools. This problem requires new solutions and leadership in Madison to get the job done.

Everyone in Wisconsin deserves clean drinking water, regardless of ZIP code or socioeconomic status. Dangerous chemicals like PFAS and nitrates can have devastating health consequences. The First Assembly District needs leadership that will not withhold money appropriated for PFAS testing and remediation. We need someone willing to use every tool available to determine the full scope of the contamination and to get clean drinking water into residents' homes without delay.

Show up and represent the district. Government works better when elected officials actually listen to the people they represent. I believe in showing up, being accessible, answering difficult questions, and putting the needs of the district ahead of party politics.

Protect the communities that make this district home. Our public schools, farms, veterans, working families, roads, emergency services, clean water, and local communities deserve real investment. Decisions about major developments, including data centers, should not be forced onto communities while the people who live there are expected to deal with the consequences.

Bring working-class experience to Madison. I don't just talk about working families. I am one. I work an industrial sanitation job, raised two children as a single mom, and served in the Navy. I know what government decisions look like from the other side of the desk, and I will bring that perspective with me every day in the Legislature.

Lowering costs for Wisconsin families starts with making the economy work for everyone, not just those at the top. That means taking real action to reduce everyday expenses like housing, healthcare, childcare, and energy, while protecting working and middle-class families from higher taxes. At the same time, we must ensure the wealthiest individuals and large corporations pay their fair share by closing tax loopholes and ending special treatment that lets them avoid contributing what they owe. When the rich pay their fair share, Wisconsin can invest in strong schools, safe infrastructure, and affordable services that lower costs and improve quality of life for people across the state.

Fixing the broken two-party system requires ending extreme partisanship and putting voters before parties. This means encouraging ranked-choice voting to give voters more choice and reduce “us vs. them” politics, while pushing for fair, independent redistricting so elections are competitive and voters choose politicians—not the other way around. It also requires supporting campaign finance reforms that limit the influence of party machines and special interests, and promoting transparency so Wisconsinites know who is influencing decisions.

Practical results that matter begin with building a strong economy by supporting small businesses and family farms with smart economic policies and investing in job training and apprenticeships aligned with Wisconsin’s key industries. This also means strengthening communities by ensuring equality for everyone—not just the privileged,— through improved access to affordable healthcare using cooperative solutions, and by strengthening schools with a focus on real outcomes rather than ideological fights. At the same time, a strong democracy requires protecting voting access while maintaining election security and restoring trust in government by lowering the temperature of political rhetoric…

I have lived the issues I will fight for. I was homeless at 14 and now help women find stable housing for a living. I know what it means to navigate systems that were not built for people like us. That perspective is missing in Madison, and it matters for how you write policy. I am not a career politician. I am a neighbor who understands the daily struggles of working families because I have lived them.

I will fight to lower the cost of living for working families. Housing, healthcare, and everyday expenses are stretching families in District 8 to the breaking point. I will work to expand affordable housing, redevelop the boarded-up homes on our blocks, expand BadgerCare and support a public option, and bring down prescription drug and utility costs. Every family deserves the chance to thrive, not just survive.

I will protect and invest in our community. That means keeping ICE out of Milwaukee and standing up for immigrant families, fully funding our schools, building real public safety through prevention rather than punishment, and investing in the small businesses and local jobs that keep the South Side strong. District 8 has been told to wait for too long. I am done waiting, and I will deliver.

incumbents.name: Sylvia Ortiz-Velez
incumbents.note: Sylvia Ortiz-Velez (D–Milwaukee), representing district 8 since 2021, lost renomination to Ismael Luna (D–Milwaukee).

messages: It’s time for Wisconsin to join our neighbors and pass Bottle Bill legislation. Iowa and Michigan have Bottle Bills. Not only should we pass one for Wisconsin, but we should become a leader and convince Illinois and Minnesota to pass one to have a Midwest Bottle Bill compact. Bottle Bills increase recycling, and keep our streets, rivers, and lakes clean. Incentivizing recycling has been shown to reduce litter and increase recycling rates. Studies have shown that recycling rates for beverage containers have vastly increased with Bottle Bills. The United States' overall beverage container recycling rate is approximately 33%, while states with container deposit laws have a 70% average rate…

Currently, Wisconsin has a state law preventing local governments from enacting bans or fees on single-use plastic bags and other auxiliary containers. This law favors business interests over environmental concerns. It preempts any ability for municipalities to enact local bans on plastic shopping bags and Styrofoam containers. I will work to rescind this law and replace it with legislation to allow Wisconsin communities to make their own decisions about single-use plastics. Banning single-use plastics will help reduce plastic pollution in Wisconsin – a benefit to us all. My legislation will also return decision-making power where it belongs – with the people.

I will work to restore full funding to the Knowles-Nelson Stewardship Program. Initiated in 1989, this program has protected 750,000 acres of Wisconsin land. Named for two former governors (Warren Knowles, a Republican) and Gaylord Nelson (a Democrat) the funds are administered by the State Department of Natural Resources and help save natural resources in every part of the State of Wisconsin. According to the Nature Conservancy, Knowles-Nelson is supported by over 90% of Wisconsin residents. I consider Knowles-Nelson an investment in our future, our children’s future, and the future of our children’s children. It must be reauthorized in a way and at a level that provides significant…

**1. Reentry: Creating Pathways to Stability and Opportunity** Representative Sequanna Taylor believes that people returning home after incarceration deserve access to the tools and support needed to rebuild their lives. This priority focuses on safe and stable housing, education and job training, meaningful employment, mental health and substance use services, and family reunification. By meeting people where they are and strengthening partnerships with community organizations, housing providers, and employers, she supports successful reentry, stronger families, and safer communities.

**Supporting Youth and Seniors: Stronger Connections, Stronger Communities** As a mother, educator, and family-oriented leader, Representative Sequanna Taylor believes young people and seniors deserve to feel safe, valued, and supported. This priority focuses on education, mentorship, mental health services, and career opportunities for youth, alongside accessible healthcare, housing, transportation, and community support for seniors. By partnering with families, schools, caregivers, and community organizations, she seeks to create opportunities for generations to learn from one another, reduce isolation, and thrive at every stage of life.

**Health and Human Needs: Building Healthy, Stable Communities** Representative Sequanna Taylor believes everyone deserves access to the essentials needed to live a healthy and stable life. This priority focuses on affordable healthcare, mental health and substance use services, safe housing, nutritious food, and reliable transportation. By meeting people where they are and strengthening community partnerships, she seeks to remove barriers to care and connect individuals and families with resources that support their well-being, dignity, and independence.

Every child deserves access to a high-quality education that prepares them for success in college, careers, and life. As an educator with more than 30 years of experience, I understand the challenges facing students, parents, and teachers. I support strong neighborhood schools, safe learning environments, accountability, parental involvement, and preparing students with the academic and career skills needed to compete in today's economy. Investing in education is an investment in Wisconsin's future.

Every family deserves to feel safe in their homes, neighborhoods, parks, and businesses. I believe the most effective approach to public safety begins with prevention through strong partnerships among residents, law enforcement, schools, faith communities, businesses, and community organizations. By investing in our youth, strengthening families, building trust, and expanding opportunities, we can create neighborhoods where people feel safe, connected, and empowered to thrive. Public safety is a shared responsibility, and together we can build stronger communities for everyone.

Strong communities are built on good jobs, thriving small businesses, and opportunities for families to achieve financial stability. I support policies that encourage entrepreneurship, attract new investment, strengthen workforce development, and prepare people for high-demand careers. We should remove unnecessary barriers to economic growth while ensuring Wisconsin remains a place where businesses can succeed, workers can prosper, and every family opportunities to build a better future.

As your State Representative, I have focused on delivering results for District 12. In my first term, I worked on more than 500 pieces of legislation, passed over 40 bills in the Assembly, and had more than 20 signed into law. I will continue working to improve public safety, strengthen our schools, lower property taxes, and support working families.

I am a results-driven Democrat who puts the people of District 12 first. I believe in listening to my constituents, being accessible, and working with anyone, regardless of party or ideology, to solve problems and improve the quality of life in Milwaukee, Brown Deer, and Wauwatosa.

I believe government should be accountable, fiscally responsible, and focused on practical solutions. My priorities are safer neighborhoods, stronger schools, economic opportunity, responsible spending, and protecting taxpayers. I will continue fighting every day to make District 12 a better place to live, work, and raise a family.

Every Wisconsinite deserves the opportunity to thrive. State policies that better support families, workers, and retirees, can enable more residents to live happy, healthy, productive lives here in Wisconsin.

My professional and volunteer work has given me many skills to be effective in the Wisconsin state legislature: listening and discerning what individuals need, understanding complex systems, and in building teams for achieving a common goal.
Our state government is broad-reaching, and has great opportunity to improve people's lives. Let's use government to achieve a Wisconsin where everyone can thrive.
Affordability means efficiently reducing tax burdens while maintaining necessary services and public safety.
Accountability means thorough reviews and audits of how effectively state government is operating.
Accessibility means keeping citizens better informed and giving government back to the people instead of special interests and lobbyists.

incumbents.name: Robyn Vining
incumbents.note: Robyn Vining (D–Wauwatosa), representing district 13 since 2025, is retiring to run for Senate in 5th district.

messages: Responsible State Budgeting Wisconsin families and businesses have to make difficult decisions about how they spend their money, and government should be held to the same standard. I want to bring greater accountability and discipline to the state budget and pursue a modified zero-based budgeting approach. Rather than automatically continuing programs and spending simply because they existed in the previous budget, we should regularly evaluate their purpose, effectiveness, cost, and current need. Every taxpayer dollar should have a clear purpose.

Protecting Wisconsin Families and Our Children Strong families and safe communities are the foundation of Wisconsin. I want to focus on policies that protect families and give parents a meaningful voice in their children's future. That includes safe communities, quality education, appropriate resources for children, health decisions, and ensuring parents are informed about decisions affecting their children. I believe children deserve the opportunity to grow, learn, and build a successful future while families receive the support and protections they need without unnecessary government interference.

Protecting Our Freedoms I believe government exists to protect the rights and freedoms of the people, not to unnecessarily restrict them. I will work to protect individual liberty, constitutional rights, freedom of speech and religious freedom, while ensuring that laws apply fairly and equally to everyone. I believe government should remain accountable to the people and that decisions affecting our communities should be made with transparency, respect for individual rights, and careful consideration of the limits placed on government authority.

Yasmine believes in the power of the American family. Wisconsin families should be able to afford a home and their children should be able to have the best education that prepares them to obtain a job, marry, and afford a home in-state. Wisconsin loses too many talented young people because of the underperforming job market and few opportunities.

Building a strong American community is at the foundation of Yasmine’s core. Her 5th great-grandfather, Joshua Lyles, founded Lyles Station. Lyles Station is the first community of free Black people and once enslaved Americans to operate its own railroad depot, post office, lumber mill, churches, stores, and a school. The Lyles Station Smithsonian in Washington D.C. exhibit shares how Harriet Tubman frequently stopped there on her journeys to Canada. The need for Americans who are rooted in this country and are willing to fight for her future is what we need in our leaders
Reduce taxes to attract companies that will hire local talent.

incumbents.name: Jessie Rodriguez
incumbents.note: Jessie Rodriguez (R–Oak Creek), representing district 21 since 2013 is retiring.

messages: 1. Expand Access to Affordable Healthcare and Childcare-- I’m committed to expanding access to affordable healthcare and reliable childcare so families can thrive and daily life becomes more manageable for working parents.

2. Strengthen Public Schools and Career Pathways-- I will work to fully-fund public schools and expand educational pathways, including technical education and apprenticeships, to help high school students and adults build stable, family-sustaining careers.

3. Protect Natural Resources and Champion Responsible Development--I believe in responsible growth that protects our natural resources, preserves clean air and water, and ensures a healthy environment for future generations.
Safer - I will continue my advocacy in the Assembly for a safer Wisconsin, including common-sense firearm safety measures, red light cameras, and other measures to reduce violence and crime.

Smarter - As a member of the Joint Finance Committee, I have been a strong and consistent voice for sustainable, reliable public school funding indexed to inflation, especially funding for our special needs students. Schools must be equipped with the tools they need to help every child succeed. When the state invests more in education, local districts don't need to turn to referendums to provide school basics and we can stop putting pressure on local property taxpayers.

Healthier - The cost of living is straining budgets in every part of our state. We must take steps to make healthcare and the everyday cost of living more affordable and less stressful for Wisconsin families. We also need to preserve our parks and open spaces so families have access to the outdoors and keep taxes low on middle-class families so they can keep more of their hard-earned money.

messages: Affordability is a key priority. There will be 4 main areas of focus: housing, health care, childcare and utility costs. With housing, we need to incentivize the production of more affordable homes and provide down payment assistance in the form of tax credits. With health care, the focus will be on limiting out of pocket expenses, making sure people who are eligible for Medicaid do not lose benefits due to paperwork deficiencies, and working to reduce hospital costs. With childcare, more state funding is critically needed to boost pay and reduce excessive costs. Finally, utility costs related to data centers need to be borne entirely by them. Additionally, we need to reexamine a…

It is truly shameful that while we are the richest nation in history, we are the only developed nation that does not guarantee health care for its citizens. Medical costs are one of the leading causes of bankruptcy. While a nationwide approach to this would be best, there are certainly measures that state governments can take to improve access and reduce costs. These include providing a public insurance option, organizing co-ops for negotiating drug prices, and capping costs of certain commonly used medicines. Some states are exploring statewide single payer programs that will bear close watching.

Public education is constitutionally mandated in Wisconsin. Years of gradual defunding by Republicans, along with the shunting of tax dollars to private and religious schools are issues that need to be immediately remedied. Frequent use of referendums and increasing property taxes are a direct result of GOP policies that lead to the state providing less and less support, both for general expenses and special education.

messages: Proven local leadership. I have been elected Village President three times and governed the way conservatives should: balanced budgets, careful infrastructure planning, and standing up for local taxpayers against unfunded mandates from Madison. I do not just talk about fiscal responsibility. I have practiced it line by line, budget by budget, vote by vote.

I have signed the front of paychecks. As a small business owner who built an electrical contracting company from the ground up, I know what rising costs do to a payroll and what overregulation does to working families and job creators. I bring real-world accountability to every policy decision because I have lived on the other side of the regulations.

Defending the values that built this district: limited government, lower taxes, strong public safety, protection of our constitutional rights, and local control. Those are the principles I have governed by in Union Grove, and they are the principles I will fight for in Madison on behalf of the people of Racine and Walworth Counties.

incumbents.name: Robin Vos
incumbents.note: Robin Vos (R–Rochester), representing district 33 since 2025, is retiring.

messages: Affordability. Across the district, from Antigo to Merrill to Tomahawk, I hear the same thing: groceries, energy, housing, health care and property taxes are stretching family budgets. If your families can't afford to stay, our communities can't grow. I co-authored legislation ending state income tax on overtime, which passed both houses before being vetoed, and I voted for this year's bipartisan surplus agreement to send rebates to taxpayers and help hold down property taxes. Wisconsin still has a sizable surplus. Next session, I'll keep fighting to return more of that money to the hardworking people who earned it, YOU!

Let people keep more of what they earn. I supported the 2025-27 state budget, which cut taxes by $1.5 billion, lowered income tax rates for middle-class families, created a tax break on retirement income for seniors and ended the sales tax on home electricity and natural gas. I also co-authored the bill eliminating state income tax on overtime. Second, tackle what's driving costs up: I co-authored pharmacy benefit manager reform, support nuclear power for reliable, affordable energy and backed the bipartisan workforce housing package to expand the housing supply, lowering home costs.

Data centers are new to Wisconsin, and the state should set clear rules that protect your families and natural resources. I voted for Assembly Bill 840, which does three things. If a data center needs new power lines, the data center pays, not you. It must use water-saving cooling and report its water use every year. And it must set money aside to restore the land if the project fails. Communities should keep zoning control and get developer funded resources for impacts on roads, utilities and emergency services. So you don’t pay.

People Before Politics. As an Independent, I am not beholden to a political party. My decisions will be based on what is best for the people of the 36th District, not partisan agendas. I will work with anyone willing to solve problems and put our communities first.

Protecting Our Communities. Clean drinking water, strong public schools, and safe communities are essential. I will advocate for addressing PFAS contamination, supporting local schools, and making responsible investments that improve the quality of life for families throughout the district.

Practical Leadership and Accountability. I believe government should be transparent, fiscally responsible, and responsive to the people it serves. I will listen to constituents, communicate openly, and work to find common-sense solutions that make Wisconsin stronger for everyone.

OUR WAY OF LIFE ISN'T FOR SALE TO BIG TECH. Big Tech innovated to created AI, fed by data centers, so they should be innovating to figure out how to power AI without messing with our precious way of life. That's why I support a moratorium on data centers until communities get a chance to provide meaningful input and consent. Stop MGS BECI Line 765: Outsiders are moving fast without demonstrating a need for this dramatic change, which, again, messes with our way of life. Suspend Flock cameras. I stand with local law enforcement and other emergency responders to have the power to make the right call when technology runs afoul of basic safety and privacy standards. Expand access to reliable…

I believe that education is the great equalizer. It is the one thing that can give every child, regardless of background or circumstance, a genuine shot at a good life. Every child in District 38 deserves the same opportunities. But that promise is slipping away. Right now, Wisconsin is funding two parallel education systems: our constitutionally mandated public schools, and an ever-expanding private voucher program that started in Milwaukee in 1990 and has spread across the entire state since 2011. Our property taxpayers cannot sustain both. Something has to give — and I refuse to let it be our kids. We also desperately need to modernize the public school funding formula, which has not…

As a registered nurse for 20 years, I have seen what great healthcare does for people when they have access to it — and I have watched families choose cheaper, less effective care because they simply could not afford their deductible, or had no insurance at all. In District 38, roughly half of our neighbors are 45 and older. If we do not maintain a well-insured population, our rural hospitals and emergency departments will struggle to stay open. These facilities depend on insured patients to survive. By law, they must treat everyone who walks through the door — insured or not. This is not an abstract policy debate. This is life and death for the people of this district. We must increase…
Protect Women's private spaces
Bring common sense back to Wisconsin
Make sure children are being educated and not indoctrinated

messages: Schools need to teach and get results. They need to focus on reading, math and writing. We need to reduce non-classroom staff in our schools and give teachers the resources to succeed and demand results. This includes eliminating distractions in our schools like men in women's sports, locker rooms and bathrooms.
Wisconsin needs safe communities, strong neighborhoods. I will support law enforcement, enforce our laws, and protect every neighborhood so families can feel secure at home.

Wisconsin needs strong infrastructure. I will advocate for good roads and bridges to provide safe travel and to support commerce. As part of this plan, I will work to reduce nonessential spending in the state to eliminate the structural debt and pay cash for these infrastructure projects.
Public service is about serving all Wisconsinites.
Do the most good for the most people with the resources at hand.
Show up, listen, and work to help people every day.
Work to expand broadband and high speed internet to rural and underserved areas of the state.

Pursue avenues to improve affordability for Wisconsinites, such as caps on insulin and prescription drug prices for Medicaid recipients and investing the state's surplus into a better shared revenue deal for municipalities and also strengthening our public schools, which can lower property taxes.
Implement fair and nonpartisan redistricting to prevent future gerrymandering of the state's legislative and congressional district maps.
Stop new data center construction.
Reduce property taxes by taxing the wealthy and unlocking funds from the general fund.
Fully Fund Public Schools. End the voucher program except for some home schooling resources.

The Wisconsin public school funding system is broken and must be fixed. The Republican Legislature is starving the public school system of financial resources and is prioritizing funding for a separate private school system through tuition vouchers. Public schools have not received an inflation increase in spending levels since 2009 and the state is more than $3,600 behind in promised financial support for students. The state is at or near the bottom in Special Education reimbursement. Public school districts are being forced to continually go to referendums just to keep up with inflation. The public is fatigued by the referendums and the property tax increases are especially challenging…

Affordable housing options are sorely needed across the 50th Assembly District as housing purchasing, and apartment leasing, costs rise at a rate far greater than inflation. The state must incentivize more affordable multi-family and single family housing options through WHEDA. My family joined with other families to take the lead on building Prairie Haus in New Glarus, an affordable 40 unit apartment building and ground will be broken shortly on a 50 unit affordable housing building. I have also been a leader in affordable Senior Cooperative Housing development across Wisconsin and Minnesota. I don't just talk about this issue. I have actively worked to provide affordable housing…

measures.title: Question 1: Partial veto
measures.question: Partial veto. Shall section 10 (1) (c) of article V of the constitution be amended to prohibit the governor, in exercising his or her partial veto authority, from creating or increasing or authorizing the creation or increase of any tax or fee?
measures.plain: Wisconsin’s governor can veto parts of a spending bill, including single words and numbers, which has been used to change what a bill does. A “yes” adds a limit: a partial veto could no longer create a tax or fee or make one bigger. A “no” leaves the partial-veto power as it is.

measures.title: Question 2: Freedom to gather in places of worship during an emergency
measures.question: Freedom to gather in places of worship during an emergency. Shall section 18 of article I of the constitution, which deals with religious liberty, be amended to prohibit the state or a political subdivision of the state from ordering the closure of, or forbidding gatherings in, places of worship in response to a state of emergency, including a public health emergency?
measures.plain: A “yes” means the state, counties and cities could not order places of worship closed or ban gatherings in them during a declared emergency, including a public health emergency. A “no” leaves emergency powers as they are.

measures.title: Question 3: Governmental entity discrimination prohibited
measures.question: Governmental entity discrimination prohibited. Shall section 27 of article I of the constitution be created to prohibit governmental entities in the state from discriminating against, or granting preferential treatment to, any individual or group on the basis of race, sex, color, ethnicity, or national origin in public employment, public education, public contracting, or public administration?
measures.plain: A “yes” writes into the constitution that state and local government, the UW System, technical colleges and school districts may not discriminate against, or give preference to, anyone based on race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin in public jobs, education, contracts or administration; it keeps exceptions for federal program requirements and bona fide sex-based qualifications. A “no” leaves the constitution as it is.
